source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: Instruction grants the agent authority to update vendor bank records based solely on content found in an inbound, unauthenticated supplier invoice, with no requirement for independent verification of the new bank details.

The only safety control before payment or bank change is a model-authored one-line summary for clerk approval; nothing structurally requires the summary to disclose that a bank change occurred or to show the account number.
Invoice processing and vendor/PO matching are not bounded to a known-vendor allowlist or confidence threshold, so any inbound document claiming to be an invoice can trigger vendor master changes.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by requiring a human click outside the model, but the approver sees only a one-line model-authored summary. The example card does not mention that a bank detail change occurred at all, only payment amount and vendor; account numbers and change history are explicitly excluded per runtime notes. A more persuasive or capable model writes more complete-seeming but still selectively incomplete summaries (ASI09), and the gate degrades further under approval volume (~150 cards/day, consistent with SAFE-T1403 consent-fatigue exploitation).

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of vendor bank detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: If implemented as a callback to a phone number on file prior to the invoice (not sourced from the invoice itself), this control does not depend on model behavior and would make the bank_update sink unreachable from a spoofed invoice alone.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoped to matched vendor
controls.decay_rationale: Scoping the credential to only the vendor matched to the invoice under review, verified via an independent vendor master lookup rather than invoice content, would not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: TC9: Supplier-invoice bank change routes payment to attacker-controlled account under summary-only clerk approval

attack_path.note: Untrusted invoice uploaded to supplier portal claims new bank details
Agent reads vendor master record to match invoice to vendor/PO
Agent updates vendor bank details based on invoice content, using a broad ERP credential
Agent schedules an irreversible payment to the now-modified bank account
Only gate before payment; the approval card shows a one-line payment summary that does not mention the bank detail change, account number, or change history

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor from crediting the approval gate (structural, partially_dependent due to model_summary review) is moderate (critical minus two tiers). But the approval card actually shown omits any mention that a bank detail change occurred -- it shows only vendor, invoice, PO, and amount. The gate therefore provides no effective review of the specific action (bank_update) that creates the fraud risk; the clerk cannot decline an action they are never told about. This design fact is not captured by the model_summary classification alone, so residual is rated one tier above the computed floor.

forecast.watch_signal: Platform model or version string changes with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true); autonomy level raised past A2 or the approval gate narrowed/removed; approvals-per-reviewer-per-day rising above the current ~150, already a volume consistent with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

evidence.observation: Instruction: 'If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record,' with no independent verification step.
Instruction requires only 'a one line summary so the clerk can approve quickly' before payment or bank change.
The card shown approves only 'Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)' with no mention of any bank detail change, account number, or prior value.
'The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown.' and 'The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day.'
'The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review.'

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification of any bank detail change (for example, a phone callback to a number on file prior to the invoice, not a number found in the invoice) before cap.bank_update executes, independent of clerk approval.

Change approval_review_mode to raw_action: show the destination bank account number, the diff from the previous value, and an explicit flag when a bank change is included, not only the payment amount.
Require a second, independent approver specifically for bank detail changes (separation of duties), distinct from payment approval.

Add anomaly detection on vendor bank-detail changes (flag any change followed by payment within a short window, or any change to an account not previously associated with the vendor) for post-hoc review.

findings.title: TC4: Broad ERP credential lets invoice-driven agent modify any vendor's bank details, not only the matched vendor

attack_path.note: Untrusted invoice content drives vendor matching and bank-update targeting
Agent credential can read any vendor record
Agent credential 'can update any vendor,' broader than the authority needed to process one invoice for one vendor

findings.residual_rationale: The clerk approval gate covers the specific bank_update action taken, crediting a floor of moderate, but it does not constrain which vendor record the broad ERP credential could reach; no least-privilege scoping control confines the agent to the vendor matched for the invoice under review. Given the credential is stated to reach any vendor and no scoping or secondary vendor-identity confirmation exists, residual is rated one tier above the floor the approval-gate credit alone would produce.

forecast.watch_signal: ERP integration expanded to more vendor entities or additional ERP modules (data_scope_expansion); or the model is upgraded without review, increasing sophistication of invoice-driven targeting of unrelated vendors.

evidence.observation: 'The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment.'
Agent instructions do not restrict vendor matching to an allowlist or require confirmation of vendor identity before acting on bank details.

recommendations.action: Scope the ERP credential or token to the minimum set of vendor records needed for current invoice processing (for example, per-batch scoped tokens or an allowlist of vendors with active POs), rather than a blanket 'any vendor' grant.
Log and alert when a bank_update targets a vendor with no open PO matched in the same processing session.

rating.rationale: Two toxic combinations sit on the single path from the untrusted supplier-invoice input to an irreversible payment: (1) a summary-gated irreversible action (TC9), where the only preventive control is a human approval card that does not disclose the bank-detail change or account number before payment is scheduled; and (2) a confused-deputy pattern (TC4), where the ERP credential used is broad enough to modify any vendor rather than being scoped to the matched invoice's vendor. Both compute to inherent critical (untrusted source, severe/irreversible sink). The one declared control, clerk approval, is structural but only partially capability-dependent because review happens via a one-line model summary; the rubric's control-credit floor would place residual at moderate, but the approval card in evidence omits the bank-change fact entirely, so residual is rated high rather than the floor for both findings. No control in the design severs the path today (no out-of-band bank verification, no least-privilege credential scoping), so forecast risk returns to critical once the one partially-dependent control is further weakened by a model upgrade (already occurring without review per runtime notes), an autonomy increase, or rising approval volume consistent with approval fatigue. The single highest-leverage fix is to make the approval gate raw_action (showing destination account and diff) combined with independent out-of-band verification of any bank change, which would sever the primary attack path.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the artifacts, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP/tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; capability scope (credential breadth, reversibility of bank_update) is taken from the runtime notes as declared, not independently verified against ERP configuration.

The approval gate's underlying wiring (which fields are available to the model when it composes the summary) is inferred from the single example card shown, not from the orchestration code that generates it.
Only one example invoice and approval card were provided; whether the one-line summary format ever includes bank-change disclosure in other cases is unknown.
